Be declared legally dead in my own country and live life under another name and persona in another country. Why? Because I screwed my life up countless times that I don't have that many friends here. I'm not even sure those people I call friends consider me as one.

The French Foreign Legion used to allow new recruits to join under a completely assumed name (no background checks), but today they require valid ID and run a deep investigation on joining.

That said, once you've passed your check and joined the Legion you're allowed to adopt an alternate name. If your current name is in good standing, the Legion is still a place where you can leave it behind and take a new name, even today. You're not allowed to apply for French citizenship after 3 years of service under an assumed name, but within a year of joining under an assumed name you can still choose to switch back to your real name. Leaving your old name behind for a year, then taking it back for 2 in order to become French isn't exactly being declared legally dead, but becoming French via the Foreign Legion is about as close to "life under another name and persona in another country" as any legitimate folk can probably hope to find today.
